title: WebMCP
description: Forms rendered with webmcp_form() and collections the MCP server exposes become callable by a browser AI agent inside the visitor's own session. Experimental: Chrome 149+ with the origin trial, and the spec is still moving.

declarativeForms.label: Agent-callable forms
declarativeForms.help: Annotate forms rendered with webmcp_form() so an agent can fill and submit them. Off, the same templates render plain forms.

readTools.label: Read tools
readTools.help: Register the MCP server's read tools for an agent on the page, calling as whoever is signed in — a visitor gets the collections whose MCP Access is Public, a signed-in user what their access groups grant. Requires the Standard edition or above, like the MCP server.

adminTools.label: Read tools in the admin dashboard
adminTools.help: Also load the read tools on dashboard pages, for an agent in your own browser. The agent reads only, even for an administrator; forms in the admin are never annotated. Off by default.

originTrialToken.label: Chrome origin-trial token
originTrialToken.help: Register this site's origin for the WebMCP origin trial at developer.chrome.com/origintrials and paste the token. It is emitted as a meta tag so visitors on Chrome 149+ get the API without a flag. Leave empty while testing with chrome://flags/#enable-webmcp-testing.
